In 1961, a Yale psychologist named Stanley Milgram tested it.
Volunteers sat at a machine with switches from 15 to 450 volts.
Every time a man in the next room got an answer wrong, they had to shock him...
But the volunteers didn't know that.
A man in a lab coat just said, "The experiment requires that you continue."
Experts had predicted maybe one in a thousand would go all the way.
Sixty-five percent pressed the final switch.
That's two out of three people!
When two other volunteers refused first, only ten percent went to the end.
